source.text: לַמְנַצֵּ֣חַ עַל־שֹׁ֭שַׁנִּים לִבְנֵי־קֹ֑רַח מַ֝שְׂכִּ֗יל שִׁ֣יר יְדִידֹֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: For the director, on Shoshannim. Of the sons of Korah. A maskil. A song of loves.

en.L: For the director: on shoshannim. Of the sons of Korah. A maskil. A song of love.
en.B: For the music director. On shoshannim. Of the sons of Korah. A maskil. A love song.
en.R: For the leader of the music. To the tune "Lilies". By the family of Korah. A song to teach and give insight. A love song.

fr.L: Au chef de chœur : sur shoshannim. Des fils de Coré. Un maskil. Un cantique d’amour.
fr.B: Au chef de chœur. Sur shoshannim. Des fils de Coré. Un maskil. Un cantique d’amour.
fr.R: Pour le chef des musiciens. Sur l’air « Les lis ». Par la famille de Coré. Un chant pour enseigner et faire comprendre. Un chant d’amour.

sw.L: Kwa kiongozi wa kwaya: juu ya shoshanimu. Ya wana wa Kora. Maskili. Wimbo wa upendo.
sw.B: Kwa kiongozi wa kwaya. Juu ya shoshanimu. Ya wana wa Kora. Maskili. Wimbo wa mapenzi.
sw.R: Kwa kiongozi wa waimbaji. Kwa sauti ya wimbo "Maua ya Yungiyungi". Wa ukoo wa Kora. Wimbo wa kufundisha na kutia ufahamu. Wimbo wa mapenzi.

decisions.choice: The title is verse 1
decisions.reason: The title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: the director
decisions.reason: As in 4:1.

decisions.choice: on shoshannim: "on lilies"
alternatives: to the tune of a song called Lilies
decisions.reason: The word means lilies (Song 2:16). It may name a tune, or an instrument; the musical sense is no longer known (69:1; 80:1).

decisions.choice: maskil
decisions.reason: As in 42:1.

decisions.choice: a song of loves: a wedding song for the king
decisions.reason: The psalm celebrates a royal wedding: the poet praises the king (verses 3-10), speaks to the bride (11-16) and promises the king lasting fame (17-18). Later readers, Jewish and Christian, also heard in it the Messiah, the coming king (Hebrews 1:8-9).

decisions.choice: to the tune "Lilies"; a song to teach and give insight
decisions.reason: Readable gives the likely sense (m2, m3).

decisions.choice: title terms for this block of psalms: "Au chef de chœur" (Literal, Balanced), "Pour le chef des musiciens" (Readable); "un cantique" for shir (Literal, Balanced), "un chant" (Readable); maskil kept as a name at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: These are the forms used for psalm titles throughout this translation, so that the titles read the same in every psalm. Maskil is a word whose exact meaning is lost; Literal and Balanced keep it as a name, and Readable gives its likely sense, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "des fils de Coré" (Literal, Balanced); "la famille de Coré" (Readable)
decisions.reason: Coré is the usual French form of the name Korah. The sons of Korah were a family of temple singers; Readable says "famille", as the English Readable says "family".

decisions.choice: "Kwa kiongozi wa kwaya" (L, B) and "Kwa kiongozi wa waimbaji" (R) for the director; "maskili" kept as a name at L and B, explained at Readable as the English Readable does, for Psalms 45-68
alternatives: "Kwa mkuu wa waimbaji" at every level
decisions.reason: These are the forms set for the whole of Psalms, so that titles read the same in every block. "Maskili" is the Hebrew word given a Swahili ending; its meaning is not certain, so Literal and Balanced keep it as a name.

decisions.choice: "juu ya shoshanimu" kept as a name at L and B; at Readable "kwa sauti ya wimbo 'Maua ya Yungiyungi'" (to the tune of "Lilies")
alternatives: "juu ya maua ya yungiyungi" at every level
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word means "lilies", but what it meant in a title is not known; the English keeps it as a name at Literal and Balanced and reads it as a tune at Readable, and the Swahili follows each level. "Yungiyungi" is the Swahili name of the lily.

source.text: רָ֘חַ֤שׁ לִבִּ֨י׀דָּ֘בָ֤ר ט֗וֹב אֹמֵ֣ר אָ֭נִי מַעֲשַׂ֣י לְמֶ֑לֶךְ לְ֝שׁוֹנִ֗י עֵ֤ט׀סוֹפֵ֬ר מָהִֽיר׃

records.literal_gloss: My heart is stirred [with] a good word; I am speaking my works to [the] king; my tongue [is the] stylus of a skilled scribe.

en.L: My heart is stirred with a good word; I speak my works for the king; my tongue [is] the pen of a skilled scribe.
en.B: A lovely theme has set my heart astir; I offer my verses to the king, and my tongue runs like the pen of an expert scribe.
en.R: My heart is full of beautiful words. I am singing this song for the king. My words flow as fast as a skilled writer can write.

fr.L: Mon cœur bouillonne d’une bonne parole ; je dis mes œuvres pour le roi ; ma langue [est] le stylet d’un scribe habile.
fr.B: Un beau thème fait bouillonner mon cœur ; j’offre mes vers au roi, et ma langue court comme la plume d’un scribe expert.
fr.R: Mon cœur est plein de belles paroles. Je chante ce chant pour le roi. Mes mots coulent aussi vite que la plume d’un écrivain habile.

sw.L: Moyo wangu unafurika neno jema; ninasema kazi zangu kwa ajili ya mfalme; ulimi wangu [ni] kalamu ya mwandishi stadi.
sw.B: Moyo wangu umejaa wazo zuri; ninamtungia mfalme mashairi yangu, na ulimi wangu unakwenda kama kalamu ya mwandishi hodari.
sw.R: Moyo wangu umejaa maneno mazuri. Ninamwimbia mfalme wimbo huu. Maneno yangu yanatiririka haraka kama mwandishi stadi anavyoandika.

decisions.choice: is stirred: bubbles over
decisions.reason: The verb (rachash) occurs only here; it seems to mean to move or bubble up, like boiling water.

decisions.choice: I speak my works: the poet speaks of his poem
decisions.reason: Only here and in verse 18 does the poet speak of himself; "my works" are the verses he has made.

decisions.choice: the pen of a skilled scribe: words that come easily
decisions.reason: A skilled scribe (Ezra 7:6) writes quickly and well; so the poet's words flow.

decisions.choice: "le stylet" at Literal
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is the scribe's writing tool; Literal names it as "stylet", Balanced and Readable say "plume", the writing tool a French reader pictures.

source.text: יָפְיָפִ֡יתָ מִבְּנֵ֬י אָדָ֗ם ה֣וּצַק חֵ֭ן בְּשְׂפְתוֹתֶ֑יךָ עַל־כֵּ֤ן בֵּֽרַכְךָ֖ אֱלֹהִ֣ים לְעוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: You are fairer than [the] sons of man; grace is poured on your lips; therefore God has blessed you forever.

en.L: You are fairer than the {{gender:children of humankind|sons of men}}; grace has been poured on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} lips; therefore God has blessed {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} forever.
en.B: You are more handsome than anyone else; grace pours from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} lips; that is why God has blessed {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} forever.
en.R: King, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are more handsome than any other man. You speak kind and gracious words. God has blessed {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} forever.

fr.L: Tu es plus beau que les {{gender:enfants des humains|fils des hommes}} ; la grâce a été répandue sur {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} lèvres ; c’est pourquoi Dieu {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}a béni pour toujours.
fr.B: Tu es plus beau que tous les autres ; la grâce coule de {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} lèvres ; c’est pourquoi Dieu {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}a béni pour toujours.
fr.R: Roi, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es plus beau que tous les autres hommes. Tu dis des paroles aimables et pleines de grâce. Dieu {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}a béni pour toujours.

sw.L: Wewe ni mzuri kuliko wana wa Adamu; neema imemiminwa juu ya midomo {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}; kwa hiyo Mungu amekubariki milele.
sw.B: Wewe ni mzuri kuliko mtu yeyote; neema inatoka midomoni {{deity_pronoun:mwako|Mwako}}; ndiyo sababu Mungu amekubariki milele.
sw.R: Ee mfalme, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni mzuri kuliko mwanamume mwingine yeyote. Unasema maneno ya upole na ya neema. Mungu amekubariki milele.

decisions.choice: you are fairer: very handsome
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled in form (yafyafita), which makes it strong: the king is beautiful beyond all others, as kings were praised to be (1 Samuel 16:12).

decisions.choice: grace poured on your lips: gracious, winning speech
decisions.reason: His words are pleasing and full of favor (Proverbs 22:11).

decisions.choice: therefore: the sign of God's blessing
decisions.reason: The words ('al ken) usually mean "therefore": his beauty and grace show that God has blessed him. They can also give the reason.

decisions.choice: children of humankind, with "sons of men" as the alternative
decisions.reason: As in 11:4.

decisions.choice: King,
decisions.reason: Readable names the one addressed.

decisions.choice: pronouns for the king follow the deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: The psalm addresses the king as "God" (verse 7), and Hebrews 1:8-9 applies verses 7-8 to Christ, so, as with the king in Psalm 2, the pronouns for the king throughout the address to him (verses 3-10 and 17-18) can be capitalized with the deity pronoun setting. The bride (verses 11-16) is not included.

decisions.choice: the pronouns for the king ("tu", "te", "ton", "tes") follow the deity pronoun setting, as the English pronouns do
decisions.reason: The English capitalises the pronouns for the king in this psalm as an option, because verse 7 calls him "God" and Hebrews 1:8-9 reads the psalm of Christ. French puts the same spans on its own pronouns, including the object pronoun "te", which English has no separate form for.

decisions.choice: pronouns for the king carry the deity pronoun setting, as in the English, but only on free pronouns and possessives ("midomo yako|Yako")
decisions.reason: The English lets readers capitalise the pronouns for the king, whom many read as pointing to the Messiah (Hebrews 1:8-9). Swahili marks "you" inside the verb ("amekubariki"), where no capital can go, so only the separate words take the span.

decisions.choice: "wana wa Adamu" at Literal, with no gender span
decisions.reason: "Wana wa Adamu" (children of Adam) is the Hebrew's own phrase and already means all people in Swahili, so the gender setting has nothing to change.

records.literal_gloss: Gird your sword on [the] thigh, mighty one, your splendor and your majesty.

en.L: Strap {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sword on [{{deity_pronoun:your|Your}}] thigh, mighty one, [in] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} splendor and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} majesty.
en.B: Strap {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sword to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} side, mighty warrior, in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} splendor and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} majesty!
en.R: Mighty king, put on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sword. Show how glorious and great {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are!

fr.L: Ceins {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} épée sur [{{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}] cuisse, héros, [dans] {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} splendeur et {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} majesté.
fr.B: Attache {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} épée à {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} côté, valeureux guerrier, dans {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} splendeur et {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} majesté !
fr.R: Roi puissant, prends {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} épée. Montre combien {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es glorieux et grand !

sw.L: Jifunge upanga {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} pajani [{{deity_pronoun:pako|Pako}}], ewe shujaa, [katika] fahari {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} na utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}.
sw.B: Jifunge upanga {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} ubavuni {{deity_pronoun:mwako|Mwako}}, ewe shujaa hodari, katika fahari {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} na adhama {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}!
sw.R: Ee mfalme mwenye nguvu, chukua upanga {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}. Onyesha utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} na ukuu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}!

decisions.choice: sword on the thigh: ready for battle
decisions.reason: A sword hung at the hip from the belt (Judges 3:16).

decisions.choice: splendor and majesty: royal glory
decisions.reason: The words (hod, hadar) are often used of God's own glory (96:6; 104:1). God shares them with the king he has chosen (21:6).

decisions.choice: your splendor: the sword, or the king's array
alternatives: gird on your splendor and majesty
decisions.reason: The words stand without a verb; they may describe the king as he arms himself, or be more things he is to put on.

decisions.choice: pronouns for the king follow the deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: As in 45:3.

source.text: וַהֲדָ֬רְךָ֨׀צְלַ֬ח רְכַ֗ב עַֽל־דְּבַר־אֱ֭מֶת וְעַנְוָה־צֶ֑דֶק וְתוֹרְךָ֖ נוֹרָא֣וֹת יְמִינֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And your majesty, prosper, ride on for [the] cause of truth and humility [and] righteousness, and let it teach you awesome [things], your right hand.

en.L: And [in] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} majesty ride on victorious for the cause of truth and humility [and] righteousness; and let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right hand teach {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} awesome [deeds].
en.B: In {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} majesty ride out to victory for the sake of truth, humility and justice; let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right hand show {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} deeds that inspire awe.
en.R: Ride out in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} greatness and win! Fight for truth, for what is right, and for those who are humble. Your strong arm will do amazing things.

fr.L: Et [dans] {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} majesté, avance victorieux pour la cause de la vérité et de l’humilité [et] de la justice ; et que {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} main droite {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}enseigne des [actes] redoutables.
fr.B: Dans {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} majesté, pars vers la victoire pour la vérité, l’humilité et la justice ; que {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} main droite {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} fasse accomplir des actes qui inspirent la crainte.
fr.R: Avance dans {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} grandeur et remporte la victoire ! Combats pour la vérité, pour ce qui est juste, et pour les humbles. Ton bras puissant fera des choses étonnantes.

sw.L: Na [katika] adhama {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} songa mbele kwa ushindi, upande [farasi] kwa ajili ya kweli na unyenyekevu [na] haki; na mkono {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wa kuume ukufundishe [matendo] ya kutisha.
sw.B: Katika adhama {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} songa mbele kwa ushindi kwa ajili ya kweli, unyenyekevu na haki; mkono {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wa kuume na ukuonyeshe matendo ya kutisha.
sw.R: Toka kwa ukuu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} ukashinde! Pigania kweli, haki, na watu wanyenyekevu. Mkono {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wenye nguvu utafanya mambo ya ajabu.

decisions.choice: prosper, ride: go out to victory
decisions.reason: The first verb (tsalach) is to succeed; with "ride" it means to ride on in triumph, as a king in his chariot.

decisions.choice: humility and righteousness
alternatives: the humble who are in the right
decisions.reason: The two words stand side by side without "and". They may name two causes, or "righteous humility". The king fights for what is true and right, not for himself.

decisions.choice: let your right hand teach you awesome deeds: your strength will show you great victories
decisions.reason: The king's own strength will lead him to deeds that fill others with awe.

decisions.choice: Your strong arm will do amazing things
alternatives: let your right hand teach you awesome deeds
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means (m3).

decisions.choice: pronouns for the king follow the deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: As in 45:3.

source.text: חִצֶּ֗יךָ שְׁנ֫וּנִ֥ים עַ֭מִּים תַּחְתֶּ֣יךָ יִפְּל֑וּ בְּ֝לֵ֗ב אוֹיְבֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Your arrows [are] sharpened, peoples under you will fall, in [the] heart of the king's enemies.

en.L: Your arrows [are] sharpened — peoples fall under {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} — in the heart of the king's enemies.
en.B: Your arrows are sharp; peoples fall beneath {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; they pierce the hearts of the king's enemies.
en.R: Your arrows are sharp. They go deep into the hearts of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} enemies, and nations fall down in front of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

fr.L: Tes flèches [sont] aiguisées — des peuples tombent sous {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} — dans le cœur des ennemis du roi.
fr.B: Tes flèches sont aiguës ; des peuples tombent sous {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} ; elles percent le cœur des ennemis du roi.
fr.R: Tes flèches sont pointues. Elles entrent profondément dans le cœur de {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} ennemis, et des nations tombent devant {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}.

sw.L: Mishale {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} [imenolewa] — mataifa yanaanguka chini {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} — katika moyo wa adui za mfalme.
sw.B: Mishale {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} ni mikali; mataifa yanaanguka chini {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}; inachoma mioyo ya adui za mfalme.
sw.R: Mishale {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} ni mikali. Inaingia ndani kabisa katika mioyo ya adui {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}}, na mataifa yanaanguka mbele {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}.

decisions.choice: arrows ... in the heart of the king's enemies: a broken line
decisions.reason: The middle phrase interrupts the picture: the arrows go into the enemies' hearts, and meanwhile peoples fall. The king is spoken of in the third person though he is addressed.

decisions.choice: they pierce (B); They go deep into (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply the verb the picture implies (m1).

decisions.choice: your enemies
decisions.reason: Readable keeps speaking to the king.

decisions.choice: pronouns for the king follow the deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: As in 45:3.

source.text: כִּסְאֲךָ֣ אֱ֭לֹהִים עוֹלָ֣ם וָעֶ֑ד שֵׁ֥בֶט מִ֝ישֹׁ֗ר שֵׁ֣בֶט מַלְכוּתֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Your throne, God, [is] forever and ever; a scepter of uprightness [is the] scepter of your kingdom.

en.L: Your throne, God, [is] forever and ever; a scepter of uprightness [is] the scepter of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} kingdom.
en.B: Your throne, God, lasts for ever and ever; the scepter of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} kingdom is a scepter that rules rightly.
en.R: God, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} throne will last forever. You rule {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} kingdom fairly.

fr.L: Ton trône, Dieu, [est] pour toujours et à jamais ; un sceptre de droiture [est] le sceptre de {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} règne.
fr.B: Ton trône, Dieu, dure pour toujours et à jamais ; le sceptre de {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} règne est un sceptre qui gouverne avec droiture.
fr.R: Dieu, {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} trône durera toujours. Tu gouvernes {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} royaume avec justice.

sw.L: Kiti {{deity_pronoun:chako|Chako}} cha enzi, Ee Mungu, [ni] cha milele na milele; fimbo ya unyofu [ni] fimbo ya ufalme {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}.
sw.B: Kiti {{deity_pronoun:chako|Chako}} cha enzi, Ee Mungu, kinadumu milele na milele; fimbo ya ufalme {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} ni fimbo inayotawala kwa haki.
sw.R: Ee Mungu, kiti {{deity_pronoun:chako|Chako}} cha enzi kitadumu milele. Unatawala ufalme {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} kwa haki.

decisions.choice: Your throne, God: the king addressed as God
decisions.reason: The plain reading is that the poet calls the king "God" ('elohim). Elsewhere the word is used of those who stand in God's place, such as Moses before Aaron (Exodus 4:16) or judges (82:6). Others read "your throne is God's" or "your divine throne". The ancient translations read it as an address, as Hebrews 1:8 does.

decisions.choice: Hebrews 1:8-9
decisions.reason: Hebrews quotes verses 7-8 as God speaking to the Son, to show that he is greater than the angels.

decisions.choice: a scepter of uprightness: just rule
decisions.reason: The scepter is the rod a king holds as the sign of his rule; a straight scepter means he rules justly (Isaiah 11:4-5).

decisions.choice: pronouns for the king follow the deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: As in 45:3.

source.text: אָהַ֣בְתָּ צֶּדֶק֮ וַתִּשְׂנָ֫א רֶ֥שַׁע עַל־כֵּ֤ן׀מְשָׁחֲךָ֡ אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֱ֭לֹהֶיךָ שֶׁ֥מֶן שָׂשׂ֗וֹן מֵֽחֲבֵרֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: You have loved righteousness and hated wickedness; therefore God, your God, has anointed you [with the] oil of joy above your companions.

en.L: You have loved righteousness and hated wickedness; therefore God, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} God, has anointed {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [with the] oil of gladness above {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} companions.
en.B: You love justice and hate evil; that is why God, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} God, has anointed {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, rather than {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} companions, with the oil of gladness.
en.R: You love what is right and hate what is evil. So God, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} God, has chosen {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} over all the others and poured oil on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} head. He has filled {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} with joy.

fr.L: Tu as aimé la justice et haï la méchanceté ; c’est pourquoi Dieu, {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} Dieu, {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}a oint [d’une] huile d’allégresse de préférence à {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} compagnons.
fr.B: Tu aimes la justice et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} détestes le mal ; c’est pourquoi Dieu, {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} Dieu, {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}a oint d’une huile d’allégresse, de préférence à {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} compagnons.
fr.R: Tu aimes ce qui est juste et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} détestes ce qui est mal. Alors Dieu, {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} Dieu, {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}a choisi plutôt que tous les autres et a versé de l’huile sur {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} tête. Il {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}a rempli de joie.

sw.L: Umependa haki na kuchukia uovu; kwa hiyo Mungu, Mungu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, amekupaka [kwa] mafuta ya furaha kuliko wenzi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}.
sw.B: Unapenda haki na kuchukia uovu; ndiyo sababu Mungu, Mungu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, amekutia mafuta ya shangwe kuliko wenzi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}.
sw.R: Unapenda yaliyo mema na kuchukia yaliyo maovu. Kwa hiyo Mungu, Mungu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, amekuchagua kuliko wengine wote, akamimina mafuta kichwani {{deity_pronoun:mwako|Mwako}}. Amekujaza furaha.

decisions.choice: anointed with the oil of joy: chosen and honored
decisions.reason: Kings were anointed with oil when they were made king (1 Samuel 16:13). Oil was also poured on guests at a feast, a sign of joy (23:5); at his wedding the king is honored above all.

decisions.choice: God, your God: or "God, your God" addressing the king again
alternatives: therefore, God, your God has anointed you
decisions.reason: "God" may be the subject, said twice for emphasis, or the first "God" may again address the king, as in verse 7. Hebrews 1:9 reads it as an address.

decisions.choice: your companions: other kings, or the king's friends
decisions.reason: He is honored above all others of his rank.

decisions.choice: chosen you over all the others ... poured oil on your head
decisions.reason: Readable says what anointing meant (m1).

decisions.choice: pronouns for the king follow the deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: As in 45:3.

source.text: מֹר־וַאֲהָל֣וֹת קְ֭צִיעוֹת כָּל־בִּגְדֹתֶ֑יךָ מִֽן־הֵ֥יכְלֵי שֵׁ֝֗ן מִנִּ֥י שִׂמְּחֽוּךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Myrrh and aloes, cassia, [are] all your garments; from palaces of ivory strings make you glad.

en.L: Myrrh and aloes [and] cassia [are] all {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} garments; from palaces of ivory stringed instruments make {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} glad.
en.B: Your robes all breathe out myrrh and aloes and cassia; the sound of strings from ivory-inlaid palaces brings {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} joy.
en.R: Your clothes smell of sweet perfumes. Music from palaces decorated with ivory makes {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} happy.

fr.L: Myrrhe et aloès [et] casse, [ce sont] tous {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} vêtements ; des palais d’ivoire, les instruments à cordes {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} réjouissent.
fr.B: Tous {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} habits exhalent la myrrhe, l’aloès et la casse ; le son des cordes, depuis les palais incrustés d’ivoire, {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} remplit de joie.
fr.R: Tes habits sentent de doux parfums. La musique qui vient des palais décorés d’ivoire {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} rend heureux.

sw.L: Manemane na udi [na] kasia [ni] mavazi {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} yote; kutoka majumba ya pembe za ndovu vinanda vinakufurahisha.
sw.B: Mavazi {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} yote yananukia manemane, udi na kasia; sauti ya vinubi kutoka majumba yaliyopambwa kwa pembe za ndovu inakufurahisha.
sw.R: Nguo {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} zinanukia manukato mazuri. Muziki kutoka majumba yaliyopambwa kwa pembe za ndovu unakufurahisha.

decisions.choice: myrrh, aloes, cassia: costly perfumes
decisions.reason: Myrrh is a fragrant resin, aloes a scented wood, and cassia a spice like cinnamon. All were rare and costly (Proverbs 7:17; Exodus 30:23-24).

decisions.choice: palaces of ivory: rooms inlaid with ivory
decisions.reason: Ivory was set into walls and furniture in the palaces of the rich (1 Kings 22:39; Amos 3:15).

decisions.choice: strings: stringed instruments
decisions.reason: The word (minni) is probably a form of the word for strings (150:4); it could also mean "from".

decisions.choice: sweet perfumes
decisions.reason: Readable names the kind of thing rather than each one.

decisions.choice: pronouns for the king follow the deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: As in 45:3.

source.text: בְּנ֣וֹת מְ֭לָכִים בְּיִקְּרוֹתֶ֑יךָ נִצְּבָ֥ה שֵׁגַ֥ל לִֽ֝ימִינְךָ֗ בְּכֶ֣תֶם אוֹפִֽיר׃

records.literal_gloss: Daughters of kings [are] among your honored [women]; [the] queen stands at your right hand in gold of Ophir.

en.L: Daughters of kings [are] among {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} honored women; the queen stands at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right hand in gold of Ophir.
en.B: Princesses are among the ladies of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} court; at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right hand stands the queen, adorned with gold from Ophir.
en.R: Daughters of kings are among the women who serve {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. Your bride, the queen, stands at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right side, wearing the finest gold.

fr.L: Des filles de rois [sont] parmi {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} dames d’honneur ; la reine se tient à {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} droite dans l’or d’Ophir.
fr.B: Des princesses sont parmi les dames de {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cour ; à {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} droite se tient la reine, parée de l’or d’Ophir.
fr.R: Des filles de rois sont parmi les femmes qui {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} servent. Ta fiancée, la reine, se tient à {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} droite, couverte de l’or le plus pur.

sw.L: Binti za wafalme [wamo] miongoni mwa wanawake {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wenye heshima; malkia anasimama mkono {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wa kuume katika dhahabu ya Ofiri.
sw.B: Binti za wafalme wamo miongoni mwa wanawake wa baraza {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}}; upande {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wa kuume anasimama malkia, amepambwa kwa dhahabu ya Ofiri.
sw.R: Binti za wafalme wamo miongoni mwa wanawake wanaokutumikia. Bibi arusi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, malkia, anasimama upande {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wa kuume, akiwa amevaa dhahabu iliyo bora kuliko zote.

decisions.choice: the queen: the king's bride
decisions.reason: The word (shegal) is a royal wife (Nehemiah 2:6). The bride of the wedding now stands in the place of honor.

decisions.choice: at your right hand; gold of Ophir
decisions.reason: The right hand is the place of honor (110:1). Ophir was a land known for the finest gold (1 Kings 9:28; Job 28:16).

decisions.choice: the finest gold
decisions.reason: Readable says what Ophir gold meant (m2).

decisions.choice: pronouns for the king follow the deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: As in 45:3.

source.text: שִׁמְעִי־בַ֣ת וּ֭רְאִי וְהַטִּ֣י אָזְנֵ֑ךְ וְשִׁכְחִ֥י עַ֝מֵּ֗ךְ וּבֵ֥ית אָבִֽיךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Listen, daughter, and see, and incline your ear, and forget your people and the house of your father,

en.L: Listen, daughter, and see, and incline your ear; and forget your people and your father's house,
en.B: Hear me, daughter, take note and listen closely: leave behind your own people and your family home,
en.R: Listen, my daughter, and pay attention. Forget your own people and your family.

fr.L: Écoute, ma fille, et vois, et tends l’oreille ; et oublie ton peuple et la maison de ton père,
fr.B: Écoute-moi, ma fille, regarde et prête bien l’oreille : laisse derrière toi ton peuple et la maison de ta famille,
fr.R: Écoute, ma fille, et fais bien attention. Oublie ton peuple et ta famille.

sw.L: Sikia, binti, na uone, na utege sikio lako; na uwasahau watu wako na nyumba ya baba yako,
sw.B: Nisikilize, binti, angalia na usikilize kwa makini: waache nyuma watu wako na nyumba ya baba yako,
sw.R: Sikiliza, binti yangu, na uwe makini. Uwasahau watu wako na jamaa yako.

decisions.choice: Listen, daughter: the poet speaks to the bride
decisions.reason: The poet now turns to the bride, addressing her as an older man would a young woman (Ruth 2:8).

decisions.choice: forget your people: begin a new life
decisions.reason: The bride came from another land (verse 13 mentions Tyre). She is to leave her old home behind and belong to the king's house (Genesis 2:24; Ruth 1:16).

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: The sentence continues in verse 12, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

decisions.choice: "ma fille" at every level
decisions.reason: The poet speaks to the bride as an older man to a young woman (meaning decision m1). French addresses someone as "fille" only with the possessive; the bare word would sound rude.

source.text: וְיִתְאָ֣ו הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ יָפְיֵ֑ךְ כִּי־ה֥וּא אֲ֝דֹנַ֗יִךְ וְהִשְׁתַּֽחֲוִי־לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: and the king will desire your beauty; for he [is] your lord, and bow down to him.

en.L: and the king will desire your beauty; for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [is] your lord, so bow down to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: then the king will long for your beauty. He is your lord; bow down to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: The king will love your beauty. He is now your master, so bow down to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with respect.

fr.L: et le roi désirera ta beauté ; car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} [est] ton seigneur, prosterne-toi donc devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: alors le roi s’éprendra de ta beauté. Il est ton seigneur ; prosterne-toi devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Le roi aimera ta beauté. Il est maintenant ton maître ; incline-toi donc devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} avec respect.

sw.L: na mfalme atatamani uzuri wako; kwa maana {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} [ni] bwana wako, basi umsujudie.
sw.B: ndipo mfalme atakapoutamani uzuri wako. Yeye ni bwana wako; msujudie.
sw.R: Mfalme atapenda uzuri wako. Sasa {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni bwana wako, basi umsujudie kwa heshima.

decisions.choice: your lord: your husband and king
decisions.reason: The word ('adon) is used of a husband (Genesis 18:12) and of a king; he is both.

decisions.choice: bow down: honor him
decisions.reason: Bowing was the sign of respect for a king (1 Kings 1:16).

decisions.choice: pronouns for the king follow the deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: As in 45:3.

records.literal_gloss: And [the] daughter of Tyre with a gift, your face they will entreat, [the] rich of [the] people.

en.L: And the daughter of Tyre [will come] with a gift; the rich of [the] people will seek your favor.
en.B: Tyre's daughter will come with a gift; the wealthiest of the people will try to win your favor.
en.R: People from the rich city of Tyre will bring you gifts. Wealthy people will want you to be kind to them.

fr.L: Et la fille de Tyr [viendra] avec un présent ; les riches du peuple rechercheront ta faveur.
fr.B: La fille de Tyr viendra avec un présent ; les plus riches du peuple chercheront à gagner ta faveur.
fr.R: Les habitants de Tyr, la ville riche, t’apporteront des cadeaux. Les gens riches voudront que tu sois bonne pour eux.

sw.L: Na binti wa Tiro [atakuja] na zawadi; matajiri wa watu watatafuta kibali chako.
sw.B: Binti wa Tiro atakuja na zawadi; matajiri kuliko wote katika watu watajitahidi kupata kibali chako.
sw.R: Watu kutoka mji tajiri wa Tiro watakuletea zawadi. Watu matajiri watataka uwatendee mema.

decisions.choice: the daughter of Tyre: the people of Tyre
decisions.reason: A city is often called "daughter" (9:15). Tyre was a rich trading city on the coast north of Israel. The words may also mean a princess of Tyre, perhaps the bride herself.

decisions.choice: entreat your face: seek your favor
decisions.reason: To entreat someone's face is to try to win their good will (Proverbs 19:6).

decisions.choice: will come, will bring
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no verb in the first half; the sense is that they come with gifts.

source.text: כָּל־כְּבוּדָּ֣ה בַת־מֶ֣לֶךְ פְּנִ֑ימָה מִֽמִּשְׁבְּצ֖וֹת זָהָ֣ב לְבוּשָֽׁהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: All glorious [is the] daughter of a king within; of settings of gold [is] her clothing.

en.L: All glorious [is the] king's daughter within; of settings of gold [is] her clothing.
en.B: The princess waits within, all splendid; her gown is woven with gold.
en.R: The princess is in the palace, and she is beautiful. Her dress is made with threads of gold.

fr.L: Toute glorieuse [est] la fille du roi au-dedans ; de montures d’or [est] son vêtement.
fr.B: La princesse attend à l’intérieur, toute resplendissante ; sa robe est tissée d’or.
fr.R: La princesse est dans le palais, et elle est belle. Sa robe est faite avec des fils d’or.

sw.L: Binti wa mfalme [ni] mtukufu kabisa ndani; mavazi yake [ni] ya nakshi za dhahabu.
sw.B: Binti mfalme anasubiri ndani, amejaa fahari; gauni lake limefumwa kwa dhahabu.
sw.R: Binti mfalme yuko ndani ya jumba la kifalme, naye ni mzuri sana. Nguo yake imeshonwa kwa nyuzi za dhahabu.

decisions.choice: within: in her room in the palace
decisions.reason: The word (penimah) means inside a building, here in her chamber before she is led out. It is not a statement about inner character.

decisions.choice: the king's daughter: the bride
decisions.reason: The bride is probably called a king's daughter because she is a princess by birth; she may also be called so as the new queen.

decisions.choice: settings of gold: gold woven or set into the cloth
decisions.reason: The word (mishbetsot) is used of the gold settings of the high priest's gems (Exodus 28:11).

source.text: לִרְקָמוֹת֮ תּוּבַ֪ל לַ֫מֶּ֥לֶךְ בְּתוּל֣וֹת אַ֭חֲרֶיהָ רֵעוֹתֶ֑יהָ מ֖וּבָא֣וֹת לָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: In embroidered [garments] she is led to the king; virgins behind her, her companions, [are] brought to you.

en.L: In embroidered robes she is led to the king; virgins [are] behind her, her companions, being brought to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.B: In bright embroidered robes she is led to the king, with her maiden companions following, brought to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.R: Wearing her colorful dress, she is led to the king. Her young friends follow her as they come to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, the king.

fr.L: En [vêtements] brodés elle est conduite au roi ; des vierges [sont] derrière elle, ses compagnes, amenées vers {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}.
fr.B: Dans ses robes brodées aux couleurs vives, on la conduit au roi ; ses compagnes, les jeunes filles, la suivent et sont amenées vers {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}.
fr.R: Dans sa robe de toutes les couleurs, on la conduit vers le roi. Ses jeunes amies la suivent et viennent vers {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, le roi.

sw.L: Katika mavazi yaliyotariziwa anaongozwa kwa mfalme; mabikira [wako] nyuma yake, wenzake, wanaletwa {{deity_pronoun:kwako|Kwako}}.
sw.B: Akiwa amevaa mavazi yaliyotariziwa kwa rangi nyingi anaongozwa kwa mfalme, na wasichana wenzake wanamfuata, wakiletwa {{deity_pronoun:kwako|Kwako}}.
sw.R: Akiwa amevaa gauni lake la rangi nyingi, anaongozwa kwa mfalme. Rafiki zake wasichana wanamfuata wanapokuja {{deity_pronoun:kwako|Kwako}}, Ee mfalme.

decisions.choice: embroidered: woven in many colors
decisions.reason: The word (riqmot) is cloth of many colors, worked with the needle (Judges 5:30).

decisions.choice: to you: to the king
decisions.reason: The poet turns again to the king; some read "to him" instead.

decisions.choice: virgins, her companions: the bride's attendants
decisions.reason: Young unmarried women went with the bride in the wedding procession.

decisions.choice: the king
decisions.reason: Readable says who "you" is (m2).

decisions.choice: pronouns for the king follow the deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: As in 45:3.

records.literal_gloss: They are led with joy and rejoicing; they enter [the] palace of [the] king.

en.L: They are led in with joy and rejoicing; they enter the palace of [the] king.
en.B: Amid joy and celebration they are escorted in, and they go into the king's palace.
en.R: Everyone is full of joy as they are led in. They go into the king's palace.

fr.L: Elles sont conduites avec joie et allégresse ; elles entrent dans le palais du roi.
fr.B: Au milieu de la joie et de la fête, on les fait entrer ; elles pénètrent dans le palais du roi.
fr.R: Tout le monde est plein de joie pendant qu’on les conduit. Elles entrent dans le palais du roi.

sw.L: Wanaongozwa kwa furaha na shangwe; wanaingia jumba la mfalme.
sw.B: Kwa furaha na sherehe wanaingizwa, nao wanaingia katika jumba la mfalme.
sw.R: Wote wamejaa furaha wanapoongozwa ndani. Wanaingia katika jumba la mfalme.

decisions.choice: joy and rejoicing: the gladness of a wedding
decisions.reason: Two words for joy are joined, as at weddings (Jeremiah 33:11).

source.text: תַּ֣חַת אֲ֭בֹתֶיךָ יִהְי֣וּ בָנֶ֑יךָ תְּשִׁיתֵ֥מוֹ לְ֝שָׂרִ֗ים בְּכָל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: In place of your fathers will be your sons; you will make them princes in all the land.

en.L: In place of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} fathers will be {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sons; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will make them princes in all the land.
en.B: Where {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} fathers once stood, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sons will stand; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will set them up as princes over all the land.
en.R: King, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sons will rule after {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, as {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} fathers ruled before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. You will make them leaders everywhere in the land.

fr.L: À la place de {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} pères seront {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} fils ; {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} les établiras princes sur toute la terre.
fr.B: Là où se tenaient {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} pères, {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} fils se tiendront ; {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} feras d’eux des princes sur tout le pays.
fr.R: Roi, {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} fils régneront après {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, comme {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} pères ont régné avant {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}. Tu feras d’eux des chefs dans tout le pays.

sw.L: Mahali pa baba {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} watakuwa wana {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}; utawafanya wakuu katika nchi yote.
sw.B: Mahali walipokuwa baba {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}}, watasimama wana {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}; utawaweka kuwa wakuu katika nchi yote.
sw.R: Ee mfalme, wana {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} watatawala baada {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}, kama baba {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} walivyotawala kabla {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}. Utawafanya kuwa viongozi kila mahali katika nchi.

decisions.choice: your fathers, your sons: the king addressed again
decisions.reason: The pronouns are masculine again: the poet speaks to the king and promises him heirs from the marriage, who will carry on the royal line.

decisions.choice: the land
decisions.reason: The word ('erets) can mean the land of Israel or the whole earth.

decisions.choice: King,; rule after you, as your fathers ruled before you
decisions.reason: Readable says who is addressed and what "in place of" means.

decisions.choice: pronouns for the king follow the deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: As in 45:3.

source.text: אַזְכִּ֣ירָה שִׁ֭מְךָ בְּכָל־דֹּ֣ר וָדֹ֑ר עַל־כֵּ֥ן עַמִּ֥ים יְ֝הוֹדֻ֗ךָ לְעֹלָ֥ם וָעֶֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: I will cause your name to be remembered in every generation and generation; therefore peoples will praise you forever and ever.

en.L: I will make {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name remembered in every generation; therefore peoples will praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} forever and ever.
en.B: I will make {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name remembered from one generation to the next; so the nations will give {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} thanks for all time.
en.R: I will make sure that people remember {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name in every age. People from every nation will praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} forever.

fr.L: Je ferai rappeler {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} nom dans chaque génération et génération ; c’est pourquoi les peuples {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} loueront pour toujours et à jamais.
fr.B: Je ferai qu’on se souvienne de {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} nom de génération en génération ; ainsi les nations {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} rendront grâce pour toujours.
fr.R: Je ferai en sorte qu’on se souvienne de {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} nom à chaque époque. Les gens de toutes les nations {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} loueront pour toujours.

sw.L: Nitalifanya jina {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}} likumbukwe katika kila kizazi na kizazi; kwa hiyo mataifa yatakusifu milele na milele.
sw.B: Nitalifanya jina {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}} likumbukwe kizazi hata kizazi; kwa hiyo mataifa yatakushukuru daima.
sw.R: Nitahakikisha watu wanalikumbuka jina {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}} katika kila zama. Watu wa kila taifa watakusifu milele.

decisions.choice: I will cause to be remembered: the poet's promise
decisions.reason: The "I" is most likely the poet of verse 2, whose song will keep the king's name alive. Some take it as God's promise.

decisions.choice: peoples will praise you: more than any king
decisions.reason: The verb (yadah) is usually used of praise to God. The words reach beyond any one king of David's line, which is why the psalm was read of the Messiah (Hebrews 1:8-9).

decisions.choice: pronouns for the king follow the deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: As in 45:3.
